name: Sanskrit Subhashitas
era: Vedic & Classical India (c. 1500 BC – 12th Century AD)
summary: Eloquent Sanskrit epigrams and poetic aphorisms celebrating righteous conduct, true knowledge, friendship, and moral courage.
bio: Subhashitas ('well-spoken words') are epigrammatic Sanskrit verses composed across millennia by poets, sages, and royal counselors. Collected in monumental anthologies like the Subhashitaratnakosha and Panchatantra, these verses served as moral compasses for daily life. Covering statecraft, friendship, the futility of greed, and the supreme sanctity of inner knowledge (Vidya), Sanskrit aphorisms present ethics not as dry dogma, but as musical, elevated art.

keyWorks.title: Subhashita Ratna Bhandagara
keyWorks.description: The supreme treasure-house anthology of over ten thousand classical Sanskrit epigrams.

keyWorks.title: Bhartrihari's Niti Shataka
keyWorks.description: A hundred classical verses on moral conduct, character, and worldly discernment.

keyWorks.title: Hitopadesha & Panchatantra Verses
keyWorks.description: Allegorical animal wisdom tales anchored in practical worldly prudence and virtue.

keyWorks.title: Chanakya Niti
keyWorks.description: Maxims of sharp political realism, ethical leadership, and pragmatic human psychology.

pillars.description: Knowledge and inner wisdom are the only treasure that thieves cannot steal and sharing multiplies.
The entire cosmos is one family — universal kinship transcending narrow parochial bounds.
Upholding truth and righteousness even when convenience, power, or fear urge compromise.
The transformative power of noble company and noble thoughts in shaping destiny.

whyTimeless: Sanskrit Subhashitas elevate daily life into a spiritual practice, reminding us that character, kindness, and truth outlast all kingdoms.
